details: U.S.-listed Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) experienced $225.2 million in net withdrawals on July 24, ending a week-long positive inflow streak. BlackRock's IBIT led these outflows, largely triggered by escalating conflicts between the U.S. and Iran and a subsequent rise in oil prices, which stoked fears of renewed inflation. Bitcoin briefly dropped below $65,000 during this period. In contrast, Ethereum ETFs continued to attract inflows.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See $225M Outflows Amid Geopolitical Tensions

details: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has initiated five task forces aimed at overhauling monetary policy, but digital assets, stablecoins, tokenization, and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) are notably absent from their stated scopes. This omission suggests that the new Fed leadership may not prioritize immediate regulatory frameworks or supportive policies for the cryptocurrency sector. Investors will be watching the task force recommendations later this year for any ripple effects on various asset classes, including crypto.
title: New Fed Chair Warsh's Monetary Policy Overhaul Excludes Crypto

details: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced on July 27 that it is holding its Singapore dollar policy band steady. The central bank projects core and headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation to remain within the 1.5-2.5% range for 2026. This decision reflects a strategic focus on stabilizing trade-dependent economic growth, with energy costs identified as a primary variable that could influence future policy adjustments.
title: Singapore Central Bank Holds Currency Policy Steady Amid Inflation
